France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 4 June 1984, in force 1 April 1985)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Monetary and Financial Code), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-57 and R.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT regime); Loi n° 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Loi n° 2017-1839 of 30 December 2017 (introducing Articles L.561-45 to L.561-49 of the CMF on the French beneficial-owner register); Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 (UBO register decree); Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD) and Décret n° 2020-1471 of 25 November 2020 as transposition; Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying fund transfers; French AML framework aligned with FATF Recommendations through GAFI membership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the natural-person beneficial owner's passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or identity authority of the shareholder's state of residence, with notarization by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961); for French documents the apostille is issued by the bureau des apostilles of the competent Cour d'appel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and current good standing of any corporate shareholder (French Kbis equivalent, excerpt of the foreign register, or certificate of active status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate shareholder's domicile (e.g., Companies House, ACRA, Hong Kong Companies Registry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account conduct, payment-history integrity and beneficial ownership, issued on the bank's official letterhead
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Anti-money-laundering compliance department of the issuing bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or notarized signature of an authorized bank officer where the bank refuses apostille; independent verification by the French formation agent is required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney ('pouvoir') appointing the French formation agent or avocat to execute the constitution formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin, or the shareholder personally before a French notary or French consular officer

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) — Articles L.210-1 to L.210-11 and L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Articles R.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); Décret n° 2024-564 (single-formality window); Décret n° 2024-565 (capital deposit rules).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI — Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via the Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises; Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) for the Kbis extract and legal registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) and the online incorporation declaration filed through the Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS (Article L.227-2 C. com.); the share capital is freely determined in the Statuts. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) opened with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the depositary issues the attestation de dépôt de fonds, and the funds are released only upon completion of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution — FR_SAS (Société par Actions Simplifiée). The founder shareholder, acting under Article L.227-2 of the French Commercial Code, (i) approves the Statuts; the share capital of EUR 1,000 is fully subscribed and paid into a blocked bank account, as evidenced by the depositary’s attestation; (ii) adopts the registered office at the address stated in the Statuts; (iii) appoints [full name] as Président for an indefinite term, with full corporate powers under the law and the Statuts; (iv) authorizes the Président to complete registration before the Guichet unique and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, to arrange the legal publication notice, and to open the company’s professional bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow deposit of share capital with a French credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Établissement de crédit agréé par l'ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution) or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) for the company under formation; transfer the subscribed cash capital; instruct the bank to issue the attestation du dépositaire (certificate of capital deposit) required for registration; the funds remain frozen until the certificate of incorporation is produced.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC declarations and source-of-funds statement
Authorization letter from the designated Président
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit, deposit with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; any error in the attestation must be cured by a corrected attestation issued by the depositary before submission to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Statuts and appointment of the Président
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Avocat / Notaire (notarial deed required only if a real-property contribution is made; otherwise private deed under Articles L.227-2 and 1317 C. civ.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (digital magazine publishing, online press and sponsored media placements), share capital allocation, management powers, and governance rules; sign the Statuts and the founder’s unanimous written decision appointing the Président; retain an original for the corporate register and a certified copy for the filing dossier.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt de fonds (when already issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any nullity risk (defective purpose, capital clause or governance clause) is cured by a unanimous rectifying decision; the corrected Statuts must be re-executed and, if already published, an erratum placed in the same JAL.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal incorporation notice in a JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d’annonces légales (JAL) habilité for the département of the registered office — official list published by the Direction de l’information légale et administrative (DILA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notice project to the JAL stating the legal form (SAS), denomination, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, name and address of the Président and the registration court; upon publication the JAL issues the attestation de parution, an essential component of the registration file.
required_dossiers: Identity of the Président and founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is incorrect, request a rectified publication (errata) without delay; a corrected publication issued before the RNE examination cures the defect and is accepted by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation dossier at the Registre National des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI and transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation form (immatriculation), upload the Statuts, the capital deposit attestation, the JAL publication attestation, the beneficial owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs), the non-condemnation declaration and criminal-record statements of the legal representatives, and pay the greffe and formalities fees online.
required_dossiers: Attestation de non-condamnation of the Président
Identity documents of the Président and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffier raises an observation, respond through the Guichet unique within 15 days and supply the rectified documents; in case of refusal, apply to the President of the Tribunal Judiciaire for an injunctive order compelling registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration at the RCS and delivery of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the dossier, the company is registered in the RNE/RCS with attribution of the SIREN and SIRET identifiers and the Kbis extract is issued automatically; INSEE, DGFiP and URSSAF notifications are transmitted automatically through the Guichet unique, and the legal existence of the SAS is evidenced by the Kbis.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If no Kbis is issued within five working days, file a formal reminder with the greffe; registration is deemed effective from the date of the Kbis, and any administrative transmission failure is cured by re-notification via the Guichet unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical, industrial and environmental compliance of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SDIS (fire services), DREAL / Direction départementale de l’environnement, CARSAT-DDETS (occupational safety) — subject matter only; no ICPE regime is triggered
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the office premises do not fall under ICPE registration; obtain the electrical conformity certificate for new electrical installations; maintain fire extinguishers and, if the premises are open to the public, complete the ERP fire-safety formalities; conclude registered waste-collection contracts for paper, toner cartridges, DEEE and batteries; prepare the DUERP before the first hire.
required_dossiers: Fire safety attestation or extinguisher maintenance certificate
Document Unique d’Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any deficiency notified by the DREAL, CARSAT or the préfecture is cured by scheduling a rectifying inspection and submitting a compliance plan within the set deadline; administrative penalties apply only if an ICPE-classified activity is unlawfully operated, which is not the case for this digital publishing activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure digital magazine publishing — no DREAL industrial authorization required; DREAL remains the future contact only if warehousing/logistics infrastructure exceeding ICPE thresholds is later operated, which is not the case for the ISIC 5813 portal activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — online press and digital publishing operate under the free-communication regime of the LCEN (Loi n° 2004-575 du 21 juin 2004); the RCS registration evidenced by the Kbis is the sole operating authorization. Optional recognition: CPPAP certificate as service de presse en ligne (tax-status benefit only, non-mandatory).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique / DREAL (Direction Régionale de l’Environnement, de l’Aménagement et du Logement) — competent for environmental registries and inspections in the registered office region
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity (online magazine publishing, editorial office and third-party IT hosting) does not appear in the categories of Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code requiring an EIA or environmental registration; no case-by-case examination required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No direct industrial discharges; office wastewater is discharged only into the public sewerage network in accordance with the municipal sanitation by-law (arrêté d’assainissement). Waste streams (paper, DEEE, toner cartridges, batteries) must be transferred to registered carriers with waste-tracking slips; data-center emissions and CSRD reporting obligations remain with the hosting providers contracted by the company.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: if the registered office is open to the public as an ERP (type R), prior SDIS inspection and préfecture clearance are required; otherwise minimum fire-extinguisher maintenance and evacuation signage apply. Electrical conformity: Consuel certificate for new installations. Occupational: DUERP registered and displayed, first-aid equipment, and emergency instructions posted; CARSAT and DDETS verify compliance during inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the professional portal impots.gouv.fr; VAT registration and electronic filing are managed through the DGFiP's online professional tax space (Espace Professionnel) and the Gérer mon entreprise / formalities portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities intending to establish a French SAS or otherwise carry on taxable activities in France must first complete company incorporation through the French business formalities portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). Upon incorporation, the French tax authorities automatically assign a SIREN number, a SIRET number for each establishment, and a French VAT identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire). For a non-resident entity not forming a French company but making taxable supplies in France, the foreign entity must apply directly to the DGFiP non-resident service (Service des Impôts des Entreprises / Service de la DGFiP) for a French VAT number using Form No. 3551 (Cerfa 15583) or the specific non-resident VAT registration procedure; the application must include proof of foreign registration, the territorial scope of activities, and expected turnover in France. In addition to the VAT number, the taxpayer must obtain the compulsory French EORI number through the customs authority (Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects) for customs transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at the entity level and is not eligible for check-the-box pass-through treatment. The only relevant elective mechanisms are the option for tax integration (régime d'intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A of the French General Tax Code, available to a French parent company owning at least 95% of qualifying French subsidiaries, and the option for the régime des sociétés de personnes which is not available to an SAS. A qualifying small or medium enterprise may elect to be taxed at the reduced corporate tax rate on its first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit under Article 205 ter CGI, but this is not a classification election. For indirect tax purposes, there is no entity classification election; VAT grouping (assujettis unis) is available under Articles 256 C and 256 D CGI but is subject to strict conditions and does not alter the entity's status as a taxable person for supplies outside the group.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Foreign suppliers of digital services to French non-taxable persons are required to register and account for French VAT from the first euro of sales under the non-established taxable person regime (Article 259 D CGI), with no general threshold for establishment-based suppliers. For small businesses established in France, the franchise en base de TVA under Article 293 B CGI exempts from VAT and from the requirement to register where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 85,000 for sales of goods and certain services, and EUR 37,500 for other services including digital publishing, unless the mini one-stop-shop (OSS IOSS/One-Stop Shop) regime is used; for digital magazine portal services B2C, the relevant threshold is EUR 37,500, but once the business supplies digital B2C services to other EU member states, the special EU OSS scheme applies and the EU-wide threshold for OSS is EUR 10,000 of intra-EU distance and digital B2C services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Since 2017, all taxpayer invoicing systems must be secured, accepted, or certified by the DGFiP under Article 289 CGI and the associated anti-fraud decree (Décret n° 2016-1091). Real-time clearance is not yet mandatory; France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and B2B transaction reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all taxable persons must be able to receive electronic invoices and must transmit transaction and payment data (données de transaction et de paiement) to the DGFiP through a registered dematerialization platform or the public portal. B2B e-invoicing on a national basis is mandatory from 1 September 2026 for all taxpayers. The new system requires structured electronic documents (Factur-X/UBL), but the fully real-time fiscal stamping model (e.g., Italian or Portuguese style) is not adopted. Existing anti-fraud software certification (NF 525 / 2031) remains applicable until mandatory e-invoicing takes effect. A digital stamping of invoices is not required; the DGFiP receives e-reporting data through certified platforms without a central real-time clearing house.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: French VAT applies to goods and services supplies. Exports of goods outside the EU are zero-rated under Article 262 CGI provided that the goods are physically delivered or transported outside the EU by the seller or on behalf of the seller and are declared for export through the French customs system. For digital publishing services, exports of services to B2B customers outside the EU are outside the scope of French VAT under Article 259 B CGI if the customer is established outside the EU and the services are not attributable to a French fixed establishment; such supplies are characterized as zero-rated/outside the scope of VAT. For B2C digital services to non-EU customers, the place of supply is outside the EU and French VAT does not apply. Advertising services and sponsored media placements supplied to non-EU customers are also outside the scope where the recipient is established outside the EU. The exporter must retain evidence that the recipient is outside the EU and, if applicable, proof of the French exporter's status as a taxable person, the nature of the services, and the absence of a French fixed establishment supplying the services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation via DELTA / DAU) with MRN registration
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Intrastat declaration if intra-EU dispatch (if applicable for goods)
Export licence or permit if the goods are controlled
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and non-application of VAT are subject to DGFiP audit scrutiny. If the exporter cannot substantiate export delivery and payment, the DGFiP may assess VAT at the standard rate, demand the VAT amount, and impose the 10% late payment penalty under Article 1731 CGI plus monthly interest at 0.20% per month under Article 1727 CGI. In cases of fraudulent intention or abusive schemes, the 80% penalty for bad faith or fraud under Articles 1729 and 1729-0 A CGI applies, together with criminal fines under Articles 1741 and 1742 CGI for tax fraud, which may include imprisonment and a fine up to EUR 500,000. Retrospective assessment generally covers a six-year limitation period (Article L.169 of the Book of Tax Procedures), extended to ten years for fraudulent behaviour. The French customs administration may also apply customs penalties under the Code des douanes for false export declarations, and the tax authority can jointly demand recovery of taxes plus penal interest and publication sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, as the French central bank within the Eurosystem; monetary and euro-system matters are governed by the European Central Bank. Foreign-exchange and cross-border payment policy is also subject to applicable European Union rules, French financial legislation, the French Treasury Directorate General, the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, and the Autorité des marchés financiers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro. The euro is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, prudential, statistical-reporting, and applicable foreign-direct-investment controls. A French SAS may generally receive foreign shareholder capital, shareholder loans, dividends, royalties, service fees, and other permitted cross-border payments without a general foreign-exchange approval. Profit remittances require distributable profits, properly approved financial statements, compliance with legal-reserve requirements, applicable withholding-tax rules, beneficial-owner and sanctions screening, and bank evidence of the underlying transaction. Dividend payments to non-residents generally do not attract French withholding tax where an applicable domestic exemption or tax treaty applies, but the exemption must be substantiated. Interest, royalties, management fees, and related-party payments require transfer-pricing support, corporate-benefit evidence, withholding-tax analysis, and documentation of applicable treaty relief. Payments to non-cooperative or sanctioned jurisdictions may be restricted or subject to enhanced controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the central bank and no mandatory conversion ratio or universal statutory deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts. Export proceeds may normally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's discretion, subject to contractual terms, accounting requirements, tax reporting, sanctions controls, AML review, and accurate recording of trade transactions. Banks may request invoices, transport evidence, customs references, contracts, and proof of economic purpose. Cross-border payment and balance-of-payments reporting may apply through banking, statistical, customs, or regulatory reporting channels, but these requirements do not constitute a general export-proceeds conversion obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional banking entity
BPCE group, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Épargne entity selected for the company

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; capital-deposit availability subject to entity and branch acceptance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale or the relevant Crédit Mutuel group entity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payments and collection; low as the sole banking solution for incorporation capital, regulated escrow, tax payments, payroll, and complex treasury. A French SAS may use an EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution under passporting rules, subject to the provider's French servicing model, safeguarding framework, transaction limits, SEPA connectivity, beneficiary verification, and AML policy. An offshore digital EMI without EU authorisation, passporting, or a regulated correspondent relationship cannot lawfully provide ordinary payment-account services to the company merely through an online interface. EMI safeguarded funds are not equivalent to bank deposits and generally do not provide deposit-guarantee protection. Stripe and AdSense-type collection or payout accounts should be treated as commercial payment platforms, not substitutes for a primary French corporate bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted after reliable electronic identification and verification of the company, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorised signatories, business activity, and source of funds. In practice, a bank may require a video interview, certified or apostilled identity documents, a French address, an in-person appointment, or an original-signature package, particularly where directors are non-resident, the ownership chain is foreign, the company is newly incorporated, or the business involves substantial international flows. A notary or bank capital-deposit process may impose separate identification and document-delivery requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders and a recently incorporated SAS with no French operating history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified identity documents; proof of residential address; curriculum vitae and professional background; French registry extract or draft incorporation documents; articles of association; shareholder register; beneficial-owner filing evidence; board or shareholder resolution authorising account opening; business plan; first-year budget; expected transaction profile; and evidence of French commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, trusts, foundations, or a multi-tier foreign holding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; certificates of incorporation and good standing for every intermediate entity; constitutional documents; registers of directors and shareholders; trust or foundation instruments where relevant; notarised or certified translations; beneficial-owner declarations; and a written explanation of control rights and economic ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained inbound shareholder funding, intercompany loans, or capital injections from third-party accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; shareholder and board approvals; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; audited accounts or tax returns of the funding party; bank statements; payment trail from the beneficial owner's account; purpose-of-payment narrative; capital-deposit evidence; and tax or legal analysis of the funding instrument.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital publishing, advertising, platform, or payment flows inconsistent with the stated low-risk business model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business description; website and application links; customer and supplier contracts; advertising insertion orders; publisher and platform agreements; Stripe and Google payment statements; invoice samples; expected monthly volumes; countries of counterparties; refund and chargeback procedures; content-moderation controls; and explanation of any restricted, political, adult, gambling, crypto, or user-generated content exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border receipts from advertising networks or payment processors with fragmented remitter names
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Processor agreements; merchant or publisher account ownership evidence; remittance reports reconciling each payout to invoices or platform statements; transaction-level ledgers; settlement-account details; tax identification information; reconciliation policy; and written explanation of payment aggregation and netting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned, high-risk, embargoed, or unusual jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due diligence; sanctions-screening records; end-use and end-user statements; underlying contracts and invoices; shipping or service-delivery evidence; legal review of EU and French sanctions; beneficial-owner verification; and documented escalation and approval controls. Transactions prohibited by sanctions must not be processed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party royalties, management fees, data services, or advertising charges lacking commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; benchmarking or pricing support; deliverables; timesheets or service evidence; invoices; withholding-tax and treaty-relief analysis; board approval; benefit analysis; and accounting reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to provide a stable French registered office, operating address, tax profile, or authorised signatory evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; registered-office agreement; lease or domiciliation contract; French tax identification evidence; director mandate; specimen signatures; corporate resolutions; utility or equivalent address evidence; and explanation of remote-management arrangements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in capital to the French bank's dedicated capital-deposit account before SAS incorporation or before a documented capital increase, using the subscriber's verified account and a payment reference identifying the company, subscription, and capital-deposit purpose. The bank or notary should receive the draft articles, subscription schedule, shareholder resolution, identity and beneficial-owner documents, and source-of-funds evidence. After incorporation or capital increase, obtain the deposit certificate and transfer the funds to the operational account. For subsequent equity funding, use a formal subscription or contribution agreement and ensure the corporate resolutions, amended articles where required, registry filings, and accounting entries match the wire. For shareholder loans, route funds directly from the lender's verified account under an executed loan agreement and classify the transfer correctly. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments and SWIFT for non-euro payments; include accurate remitter, beneficiary, IBAN, BIC, legal name, registered address, and purpose information. There is no universal French statutory purpose-code list equivalent to certain controlled-currency jurisdictions; the bank's payment-purpose, regulatory-reporting, and AML classification must be completed truthfully. Avoid third-party funding, cash deposits, unexplained round-tripping, or split payments designed to evade review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro settlements within the SEPA framework. Use SWIFT cross-border payment messaging, commonly an MT103 customer credit transfer or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or non-euro payments; confirm correspondent-bank charges, value date, sanctions screening, beneficiary details, and payment repair procedures. Commercial letters of credit may be issued or advised through a relationship bank for qualifying goods transactions, although a digital magazine business will more commonly use open-account settlement, card acquiring, direct debit, or documented bank transfers for software, cloud, content, advertising, and professional services. Maintain purchase orders, contracts, invoices, delivery or service evidence, customs documents where goods are involved, tax treatment, supplier due diligence, and approval records. For intra-group payments, retain transfer-pricing and beneficial-owner documentation. French and EU payment rules do not generally require pre-clearance of ordinary current-account payments, but banks may suspend or reject transactions for AML, sanctions, fraud, insufficient information, or correspondent-bank restrictions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot EUR/foreign-currency conversion through an authorised bank or regulated investment firm.

Deliverable forward exchange contracts for identified and documented commercial exposures, subject to bank suitability, credit-limit, collateral, confirmation, accounting, and, where applicable, MiFID II and EMIR requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local convertibility or settlement restrictions, where offered by an appropriately authorised counterparty and legally permissible in the relevant currency jurisdiction; NDFs are generally unnecessary for ordinary EUR exposures.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for documented funding or recurring currency exposures, subject to counterparty eligibility, legal documentation, collateral, valuation, accounting, and EMIR obligations where applicable.

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and other structured hedges only after suitability, product-governance, cost, leverage, early-termination, and downside-risk review; speculative trading unrelated to the company's underlying exposure should be prohibited under the treasury policy.

SEPA cash concentration, multi-currency bank accounts, automated sweeps, and internal netting may be used for liquidity management, provided intercompany balances, interest, transfer pricing, legal capacity, and payment-services restrictions are documented.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approval and filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the INPI single filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve within six months after the financial year-end; file within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically. For a 31 December year-end, filing is generally due by 31 July on paper or 31 August electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The court may order filing under a daily penalty payment and impose a civil fine on the legal representative. Persistent non-compliance may result in registry enforcement measures and administrative removal procedures; no automatic fixed strike-off date applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for financial years ending on 31 December; electronic filing is mandatory.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, and possible tax audit or assessment. Deliberate or repeated non-compliance may generate additional penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual CA12 filing is generally due by the second business day after 1 May for eligible simplified-regime taxpayers; taxpayers under the normal regime file monthly or quarterly CA3 returns instead.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, and potential tax assessment. Repeated failures may lead to enhanced penalties and enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information confirmation and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the INPI single filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: France does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation. UBO information must be accurate and updated within 30 days after any change, and supporting information must be produced upon request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may result in criminal penalties, judicial orders, and registry compliance action, including possible administrative removal proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate decisions and statutory minute-book completion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No routine filing authority; records must be maintained by the SAS and produced to competent authorities when legally requested
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Complete shareholder approval and corporate decision records within the six-month annual accounts approval period, subject to the SAS articles and applicable Commercial Code requirements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or missing corporate records may impair the validity or evidential value of decisions and expose the company and officers to civil, tax, or regulatory consequences.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of the applicable thresholds: EUR 5 million total balance sheet assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Mandatory appointment may also arise from group-control relationships or other statutory conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (Autorité des normes comptables), with IFRS permitted or required in specific reporting contexts; statutory accounts of an SAS are generally prepared under French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO certification is required solely because a year has elapsed. The SAS must identify and report its beneficial owners, update the filing within 30 days of any change, and maintain evidence supporting ownership and control. Share transfers must be recorded in the register of movements of securities and reflected in shareholder records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or individual shareholder accounts
Minute book of shareholder and corporate decisions
Register of directors and corporate officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300-1,200 per year for a standard registered-office or domiciliation service; higher where mail handling, premises access, or additional corporate services are included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000-12,000 per year for a small, non-complex SAS; fees increase materially with mandatory group reporting, regulated activities, international operations, or significant transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs; standard 25% thereafter; 3.3% social surcharge for groups with turnover exceeding €250 million; R&D Tax Credit ('CIR') at 30% of qualifying R&D up to €100 million and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit ('CII') for SMEs at 20% of eligible innovation expenditures up to €400,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual results declaration via the 'liasse fiscale': primary Form 2065-SD and supporting schedules 2052-SD to 2069-SD; mandatory electronic filing through impots.gouv.fr's 'Échange de Formulaires Informatisé' (EFI) / TéléTVA portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing; corporate income tax pre-payments are made in four quarterly instalments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, file no later than the second working day following 1 May. For off-calendar fiscal years, file no later than the third month after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: French corporate identification number, legal form (SAS), registered office address and APE/NAF activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned SAS must state the French SIREN/SIRET and a physical French registered address; no foreign-code designation is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or deficit for the year before set-off of prior losses, after tax adjustments (add-backs and deductions) reported on Schedule 2053-SD.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute pure French tax residence result; no branch allocation applies because the SAS is a French resident corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses carried forward and offset against the current-year taxable profit within the statutory cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred by the French SAS under French tax rules may be carried forward; losses from foreign parent companies cannot be offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annexe 2065-SD, 'Répartition de l'impôt sur les sociétés'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of final CIT, application of the reduced rate band, the 25% standard rate, any social surcharge and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not individually identified in the IS return; only the SAS legal representative signs the declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of R&D and innovation tax credits (CIR/CII) that reduce the corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SAS may claim CIR/CII only for qualifying research and innovation performed by French-based employees or subcontractors in France/EEA; foreign-affiliate activities do not qualify.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a statutory increase of 10% of assessed tax if the return is filed after the grace period, 40% for bad faith and 80% for fraud; late-payment interest accrues at 0.4% per month (Article 1727 CGI); each omitted schedule may incur a separate fixed penalty of €150 and a late-filing surcharge applies after formal notice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before the dividend payment date, the non-resident shareholder must supply the French paying company with an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, accompanied by a written beneficial-ownership and residence declaration. Where treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief is sought, the standard French administrative form for reduced withholding is Form No. 5000 (or its electronic equivalent via impots.gouv.fr), which is retained in the payer's audit file. If excess withholding has been applied, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the local French tax office (SIE) using the ordinary remedying period set out in Article R.196 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding tax of 33.33% generally applies to patent, copyright and similar IP royalties paid to non-residents without a French permanent establishment; the rate is commonly reduced to 10%, 5% or 0% under tax treaties and, for associated EEA companies, to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive. Interest: domestic law generally imposes no withholding tax on qualifying bank or intra-group loan interest paid to a non-resident company; however, a 75% withholding tax applies to payments to entities established in non-cooperative tax jurisdictions (NCST) unless the fraud/sham exception is satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (annual consolidated group turnover or balance-sheet total of the ultimate parent), triggering mandatory preparation of the French Master File and Local File. Below the threshold, no annual pre-filed TP documentation is required, but the SAS must be able to produce a full arm's-length file upon tax audit; failure to produce the file when formally requested attracts a penalty of 0.5% of the value of the undocumented related-party cross-border transactions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as a standalone regime, but the 'abus de droit' doctrine (Article L64 LPF), the GCC/BEPS anti-conduit case law and French beneficial-ownership rules require genuine French economic substance. The SAS must maintain its real seat of management, local board decisions, personnel, premises and business risks in France; otherwise it may be treated as a fictitious letterbox entity, stripped of treaty protection and reassessed with 80% penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting or materially understating digital magazine advertising and sponsorship revenues on the 2065-SD return; issuing or using fictitious invoices; creating undisclosed offshore sales accounts; intentionally hiding the beneficial owner of the SAS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment of unpaid CIT plus 40% bad-faith penalty and 0.4%/month late-payment interest; 80% abuse-of-law penalty where concealment is established. Criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI exposes individuals to up to 5 years' imprisonment and a €75,000 fine; legal entity fines are quintupled under Article 131-38 of the French Penal Code, with possible compulsory winding-up and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or de facto manager who signed the false return is prosecuted as perpetrator and may be sentenced to a management ban (interdiction de gérer), an order prohibiting exit from French territory, confiscation of personal property, joint and several liability for the evaded tax and all consequential interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Conduit (Société Fictive and Abus de Droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing the French SAS as a letterbox between foreign shareholders and advertisers with no genuine office, employee, business risk, counterparty contract or substantive decision-making in France; diverting advertising revenue through the conduit solely to avoid French corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may disregard the artificial structure under Article L64 LPF, tax the real economically substantive beneficiary in France and apply a penalty of 80% of the avoided tax (or 40% where no bad-faith intent is proven). Cross-border DAC6/DPR filing obligations carry a separate €10,000 penalty for each unreported tax-relevant arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil and impose joint civil liability on the ultimate owner and officers for unpaid French taxes, trigger an interdiction de gérer, freeze personal assets, prohibit exit from France and apply the Article 1741 criminal penalties in aggravated fraud cases.
